card.name: Haka
card.tagline: Aotearoa New Zealand — Māori chant and challenge. The ground itself answers.
card.profile: Haka (; singular and plural haka, in both Māori and New Zealand English) are a variety of ceremonial dances in Māori culture. A performance art, haka are often performed by a group, with vigorous movements and stamping of the feet with rhythmically shouted accompaniment. Haka have been traditionally performed by both men and women for a variety of social functions within Māori culture. They are performed to welcome distinguished guests, or to acknowledge great achievements, occasions, or funerals. Kapa haka groups are common in schools.
card.insight: Prince Alfred, the Duke of Edinburgh, was the first royal to visit New Zealand, in 1869. In September 2024, thousands gathered in Eden Park in Auckland to break the record of the largest haka performance.
